items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-27
items.q: And then that's when Lou Forbes took hold of me and started teaching me to stand up when I play.

ctx.x: Well, did they have any fakers out there? No?

No, they were all readers. They played overtures and things like that. Overtures and played, that's how I got to know all this crap. I mean, in fact, when I went to this, when I was in high school, I got a job at the Liberty Theater as an usher working just weekends in high school during the school season. I think we got a dollar or two dollars a day. And you'd always get tips on Saturday and Sunday when you'd have an over crowd of people and you'd get people to sit. You have one of these flash boxes with green…
That's a trick. They don't know that you made a mistake.

So the people applauded, and just about when they stopped applauding, they started applauding again. So Lou Forbes comes out, and he's taking a bow, and he's telling you guys, come on outside and take a bow. We stand about a footwork, taking a bow. But they don't know that they're not clapping for us, they're clapping for Roosevelt's picture, the American flag, that's in back of us. This is a funny story. This is from 1933. Here's some names you'll remember. Frankie Masters? No. Now this was at the Sanger Theatre.
And you worked with who at the Sanger? I worked with Forbes. Forbes?

items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-11-10
items.q: And Lou Forbes was conducting, and then we got a normal applause hand after we were finished playing.

ctx.x: Not that I remember. You only talked about the Sam of Pops.

This was the first March of Dimes when Roosevelt was alive. It was the March of Dimes was set up in his honor because of his, his affliction and his polioids. And it was there with Lou Forbes. He was, we were at the Roseville Hotel then. And they had, on stage, they had a regular backdrop on it. And Lou Forbes was conducting, and then we got a normal applause hand after we were finished playing. And as we were getting off the stage for the next band, our show actor was coming on, it started a tremendous amount of…
Yes. My real name is Curtis D. Jerdy. Okay.
